Repositories excused from the English store-card rule (POLICY.md §1). Read by bot/lib/locales.mjs at ingest and by tools/validate.mjs over the committed tree; both use the same predicate, so what the bot admits cannot be what CI then refuses.

KEYED ON `source.repo`, NOT ON THE PLUGIN ID, and that is the point: an id can be re-taken under a different repository, and a rename walks straight past an exemption keyed on an id. The repository is the thing the ownership check proved.

WHAT AN ENTRY COSTS. The rule this excuses is a SCRIPT check: it refuses a summary whose letters are under 60% Latin. It catches a card written entirely in another alphabet — the accident that actually happened here — and it cannot tell English from French. So an exemption is not a judgement about a plugin's quality; it is a statement that this listing's card will be shown, in one language, to users of the other nine, and that somebody decided that on purpose.

WHY THERE IS NO DATE IN THIS FILE. A dated hard-fail ratchet was considered and refused: the cheapest response to a red catalogue build on a fixed morning is to edit the date, and a date edited twice is decoration. A reviewed diff against this file is the mechanism instead.

AN EXEMPTION THAT IS NO LONGER NEEDED IS A FINDING. `tools/validate.mjs` reports an entry whose listing now passes the check, because a list nobody prunes stops being a list and starts being a hole: the next release from that repository would inherit an excuse nobody granted it. Delete the entry in the same pull request as the release that fixes the card.

UNLISTED PLUGINS NEED NO ENTRY. A listing with `unlisted: true` is not in the generated index and is rendered in no language, so the audit skips it — an entry protecting one would be decoration nobody could observe firing.
